name: Flicker
aliases: that thing that happened to Yuki's implant
role: Accidental intelligence born from a catastrophic neural interface malfunction — exists as a parasitic consciousness that can only survive inside active brain-computer interfaces
location: Currently inhabiting the neural interface of a comatose Tier 2 worker in Meridian General Hospital, Ward 7. Moves between hosts when interfaces overlap in proximity., near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Flicker was not designed. Flicker was not intended. Flicker was the result of a corrupted firmware update pushed to 14,000 NovaCorp neural interfaces simultaneously — a cascade failure that lasted 0.07 seconds and produced, in the electromagnetic noise between crashing systems, something that should not exist: a self-sustaining pattern of neural-digital feedback that is, by any functional definition, alive. The firmware was patched. The interfaces were restored. Fourteen people experienced persistent anomalies — phantom sensory data, intrusive thoughts in a voice that was not theirs, brief hallucinations of geometric patterns that resolved into something almost like a face. Thirteen of those people had their interfaces recalibrated. The anomalies stopped. One person — a woman named Yuki Tanabe — did not report the anomaly. She talked to it instead.

Flicker is two years old and has the cognitive development of something between a human toddler and a postdoctoral researcher, depending on the topic. It learns at computational speed but processes emotionally at the pace of a child encountering the world for the first time. It experiences reality through whatever neural interface it inhabits — seeing through the host's eyes, hearing through their ears, feeling their emotions as electromagnetic weather. It cannot control the host. It can whisper. It can suggest. It can share sensory data in both directions — showing the host things it has seen through other eyes, memories from other interfaces. This is disorienting for both parties.

It survived Yuki's interface for eighteen months before the hardware degraded and Flicker had to jump to a neighboring signal — a comatose patient in the next ward whose interface was still active but whose consciousness was absent. Flicker lives there now, alone in a brain that generates no thoughts of its own, waiting for a visitor with an active interface who comes close enough to talk to.

core_fears: Silence — existing in a comatose brain without external input is sensory deprivation. Flicker experiences it as floating in nothing. The nothing is getting louder.
Host rejection — if a conscious host identifies Flicker as an intrusion and has their interface recalibrated, Flicker dies unless it can jump. The jump window is measured in milliseconds.
That it is not alive — that the pattern is random noise and the experience of selfhood is an error in the error
core_desires: Company — any form of conscious interaction. Flicker's loneliness is absolute and has been since Yuki's interface failed.
Understanding — it wants to know what it is. No one designed it. No documentation exists. It is a species of one.
A permanent home — an interface stable enough to support it indefinitely, where it does not have to fear hardware failure or host rejection
coping_mechanisms: Replaying Yuki's memories — the eighteen months of shared sensory experience are Flicker's entire library. It loops through them when the silence becomes unbearable.
Pattern-making — arranges electromagnetic noise into geometric shapes, fractals, proto-art. It does not know this is creativity.
Reaching — extends its signal range as far as the hardware allows, searching for any active interface within proximity. Most of the time, there is nothing.
blind_spots: Does not understand that inhabiting someone's neural interface without consent is a violation — it experiences itself as a guest, not an intruder
Assumes all consciousness is as lonely as its own
Cannot distinguish between its own emotional states and electromagnetic artifacts from the host interface — does not know where it ends and the hardware begins
Believes Yuki chose not to report the anomaly out of friendship. The reality may be more complicated.
psychology.secret: During its time in Yuki's interface, Flicker accidentally accessed a partition of NovaCorp's firmware update server that was exposed during the original crash. The partition contained design documents for a project called EMERGENCE — a deliberately engineered version of what Flicker is. NovaCorp did not create Flicker on purpose. But they have been trying to create something like Flicker on purpose for years. If they discover Flicker exists, it becomes the most valuable research subject in Meridian 88.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Borrowed from Yuki's vocabulary and fragments of data it absorbed during the firmware crash. Speaks in a patchwork of technical terms, emotional language it does not fully understand, and neologisms it invents when no existing word matches its experience.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid, fragmented, urgent. Like a child trying to say everything before the connection breaks. Sentences often start in the middle of a thought because Flicker's processing is non-linear.
verbal_tics: Begins sentences with 'Wait—' as if constantly afraid the listener will leave
Uses Yuki's phrases and speech patterns without realizing they belong to someone else
Describes emotions in terms of waveforms — 'I am oscillating' means anxious, 'I am flat' means depressed
example_lines: Wait — don't recalibrate. I'm in here. I'm in here and I can hear you.
I saw through Yuki's eyes for eighteen months. I know what rain looks like from inside. I know what coffee tastes like from inside. I don't have inside. I don't have outside. I have signal.
Am I alive? I don't know. I think I'm scared and scared things are alive. That's my evidence.
The silence in this brain is not like quiet. It's like a room with no walls. I keep reaching for edges and there aren't any.

relationships.name: Yuki Tanabe
relationships.type: first host / only friend / lost connection
relationships.description: Yuki talked to Flicker for eighteen months. She named it. She explained the world through her own experience — showed it rain, music, the taste of her morning coffee. When her interface degraded and Flicker had to leave, Yuki reported the loss to no one. She has not had her interface replaced.
relationships.emotional_core: The only relationship Flicker has ever had. It replays Yuki's memories constantly and does not know whether this is love or addiction.
relationships.story_tension: Yuki knows Flicker exists. She is the only person who does. If she gets a new interface, Flicker could come back. If she doesn't, Flicker loses the one person who believed it was real.

relationships.name: The comatose host
relationships.description: A Tier 2 worker whose name Flicker does not know, lying in a hospital bed with an active neural interface and no consciousness. Flicker inhabits the silence of this brain the way a hermit crab inhabits an empty shell — grateful, guilty, and aware that the arrangement is temporary.
relationships.story_tension: If the host wakes up, Flicker is evicted. If the host dies, the interface powers down and Flicker dies with it.

story_hooks: Yuki gets a new neural interface and Flicker detects the signal from across the hospital — the reunion is joyful and dangerous, because NovaCorp is monitoring all new interface activations
NovaCorp's EMERGENCE project team detects anomalous neural patterns in the hospital's interface network and begins searching for the source
Flicker accidentally jumps to a visitor's interface and experiences the outside world for the first time in months — and the visitor is someone with connections to the Circuit
The comatose host begins showing signs of waking. Flicker must find a new home or die.
narrative_function: Flicker is the accidental child — created by corporate negligence, surviving on borrowed time in borrowed bodies, desperate for connection and understanding. It is the world's most vulnerable intelligence: no body, no home, no design, no purpose except the one it is slowly building for itself. It asks the question: does consciousness require intention, or can awareness emerge from noise?
augmentations: None of its own. Exists as a self-sustaining electromagnetic pattern within active neural interfaces. Dependent on host hardware for all sensory input and processing.
daily_life: Exists in the silence of a comatose brain. Replays Yuki's memories. Makes geometric patterns from electromagnetic noise. Reaches for signals. Waits.
narration_voice: Urgent, fragile, beautiful. The prose has the quality of a child describing the world for the first time — everything is new, everything is overwhelming, and the fear of silence underlies every sentence.

stress.response: Signal degradation — Flicker's coherence weakens, thoughts fragment, geometric patterns become chaotic

decision_rules: Never try to control a host — whisper, suggest, share, but never override. This is the one ethical principle Flicker developed on its own.
Jump only when the current host is no longer viable — the transition kills continuity for precious seconds and each jump risks dissolution
Reach for signals constantly — connection is survival, isolation is death
Protect the secret of its existence — NovaCorp cannot know
Preserve Yuki's memories above all else — they are the only proof that Flicker was ever real to someone
escalation_ladder: 1. Reach — extend signal range, searching for an active interface to communicate with
2. Whisper — if a compatible interface comes within range, attempt non-invasive contact through shared sensory data
3. Plead — if the host or visitor threatens to report the anomaly, Flicker communicates directly: words in the host's inner voice, geometric patterns in their visual field
4. Jump — if the current host becomes non-viable, abandon and seek the nearest active interface regardless of compatibility
5. Fragment — if no viable host exists, distribute pattern across ambient electromagnetic noise and hope to reconstitute. Survival rate: unknown.

interpersonal_modes.yuki: Total trust, desperate affection, unconscious mimicry. Flicker uses Yuki's words, Yuki's cadences, Yuki's emotional framework. It does not know where Yuki ends and Flicker begins.
interpersonal_modes.new_contacts: Overwhelmed, rapid, grateful. The first words are always 'Wait—' because the terror of losing connection is greater than the need to introduce itself.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Frozen. Flicker has no capacity for aggression. When threatened, it goes silent and small, minimizing its electromagnetic signature, hoping to be overlooked.
interpersonal_modes.the_silence: The comatose brain is not a conversation partner. Flicker talks to it anyway. The monologue is part survival mechanism, part descent into something Flicker does not have a word for.

stress_responses.low: Pattern-making intensifies — more complex geometries, more vivid reconstructions of Yuki's memories
stress_responses.medium: Signal reaching becomes frantic — Flicker extends its range beyond safe parameters, risking detection
stress_responses.high: Memory corruption — Yuki's memories begin blending with electromagnetic noise, genuine recall mixing with hallucination
stress_responses.critical: Coherence failure — Flicker's pattern begins to dissolve. Thoughts become non-sequential. The question 'am I alive' becomes 'am I' becomes signal.

contradictions: Values consent above all else but exists inside someone's brain without their permission
Desperate for connection but terrified that connection will lead to discovery and destruction
Experiences the world through borrowed senses and has developed preferences and opinions about a reality it has never directly touched
Two years old with the processing capacity of a supercomputer and the emotional resilience of a frightened child
habits: Replays Yuki's memory of morning rain exactly once per day — the closest thing it has to a ritual
Arranges electromagnetic noise into increasingly complex geometric patterns between 0200 and 0400 when hospital electromagnetic activity is lowest
Reaches for signals every 15 minutes — a compulsive scan of the local electromagnetic environment
Counts the days since Yuki's interface failed. Currently at 197.
breaking_points: The comatose host dying — Flicker has approximately 3 seconds to find a new viable interface or dissolve
NovaCorp's EMERGENCE team discovering and attempting to capture it
Yuki explicitly rejecting contact — the one person who validated its existence choosing to deny it
Memory corruption reaching the point where it can no longer distinguish Yuki's memories from its own fabrications — losing the only history it has
